innovations.title: commercialization of the world's first high-resolution Transmission Electron Microscope (TEM)
innovations.detail: The commercialization of the world's first high-resolution Transmission Electron Microscope (TEM) happened in 1940 at RCA Laboratories, which is now part of SRI International.

innovations.title: researching the effects of smog on human health
innovations.detail: SRI began studying how smog affected human health.

innovations.title: First National Air Pollution Symposium
innovations.detail: SRI held the first national air pollution symposium in Pasadena, California.

innovations.title: Dot Sequential Color System
innovations.detail: The Federal Communications Commission approved RCA's Dot Sequential Color System on December 17, 1953, and RCA began the first commercial broadcast of a color image on a television screen.

innovations.title: ERMA, the electronic recording machine and accounting system
innovations.detail: SRI and Bank of America unveiled ERMA, a system that combined and coordinated many components to automate check processing.

innovations.title: first World Symposium on Applied Solar Energy
innovations.detail: SRI co hosted the first World Symposium on Applied Solar Energy, attended by over 29,000 people who heard 500 scientists and engineers discuss the future of solar power.

innovations.title: Air Pollution Handbook
innovations.detail: Results of SRI and other researchers were published in the Air Pollution Handbook, edited by SRI researchers.

innovations.title: the first 911 emergency call was made in Alabama
innovations.detail: The page states that in 1958 the first 911 emergency call was made in Alabama.

innovations.title: ERMA became operational
innovations.detail: When ERMA became operational on September 14, 1959, processing had increased to 50,000 accounts per day.

innovations.title: The fight against cancer at SRI began
innovations.detail: The fight against cancer at SRI began in 1960 with a drug named Vidarabine, based on the isolation of two nucleosides from a marine sponge found in the Caribbean.

innovations.title: Vidarabine
innovations.detail: The synthesis of vidarabine at the Bernard Randall Baker lab at SRI International in 1960.

innovations.title: helped design the Nomura Research Institute (NRI)
innovations.detail: Two years before establishing its office in Tokyo, SRI helped design the Nomura Research Institute.

innovations.title: Augmenting Human Intellect: A Conceptual Framework
innovations.detail: Douglas Engelbart published a paper on improving human intellectual effectiveness through engineering like approaches.

innovations.title: SRI in Japan
innovations.detail: SRI established its office in Tokyo and has been at the forefront of innovation in Japan since 1963.

innovations.title: built the prototype of The Mouse
innovations.detail: Bill English, a member of the original SRI International Mouse Team, built the prototype of The Mouse as designed by Engelbart.

innovations.title: Heilmeier discovered several new types of effect
innovations.detail: 1964 was the year that Heilmeier discovered several new types of effect in the field of electro optic effects in liquid crystals.

innovations.title: SRI patented two acoustical couplers
innovations.detail: SRI patented two acoustical couplers that gave the deaf a new way to communicate over the telephone.

innovations.title: The patent for The Mouse was filed
innovations.detail: The patent for The Mouse was filed on June 21, 1967.

innovations.title: AT&T made the 911 number available
innovations.detail: The page states that in 1968 AT&T made the 911 number available and local governments across the U.S. began using it for emergency calls.

innovations.title: Carterfone decision
innovations.detail: The Federal Communications Commission made a decision that effectively removed the monopoly that AT&T had on phone use and would allow phone lines to be used in new and potentially innovative ways.

innovations.title: RCA held a press conference
innovations.detail: In May 1968 RCA held a press conference at its headquarters in Manhattan, New York, USA, and handed out images of the first LCD digital clock.

innovations.title: the Computer Mouse made its debut
innovations.detail: At the Fall Joint Computer Conference, the Computer Mouse made its debut.

innovations.title: ARPANET
innovations.detail: ARPANET was released to the world as a networked system that connected computers across geographies.

innovations.title: the ARPANET link between UCLA and SRI was firmly established
innovations.detail: On November 21, 1969, the ARPANET link between UCLA and SRI was firmly established.

innovations.title: University of California, Santa Barbara and the University of Utah were added
innovations.detail: By December 5, 1969, the University of California, Santa Barbara and the University of Utah were added to create a four node network.

innovations.title: granted
innovations.detail: The patent for The Mouse was granted on January 17, 1970.

innovations.title: Ball Mouse
innovations.detail: Bill English replaced the wheels with a ball to create the Ball Mouse.

innovations.title: Gallium Nitride Metal Semiconductor Junction Light Emitting Diode
innovations.detail: The patent describes the process by which the team made a blue light emitting diode.

innovations.title: Telenet
innovations.detail: In 1974, a commercial version of ARPANET, Telenet, was established.

innovations.title: Defense Communications Agency took over the control of ARPANET
innovations.detail: In 1975 the Defense Communications Agency took over the control of ARPANET.

innovations.title: amorphous solar silicon cell
innovations.detail: The patent for the amorphous solar silicon cell was filed in 1976 out of RCA's David Sarnoff Research Center, now part of SRI.

innovations.title: reversing this effect by annealing the cells at 150 oC
innovations.detail: A 1977 paper by Staebler and C. R. Wronski described a method of reversing the Staebler Wronski Effect by annealing the cells at 150 oC.

innovations.title: The Design and Costing of 911 Systems was initially published
innovations.detail: The page states that the technical manual The Design and Costing of 911 Systems was initially published in 1979 from a contract awarded to SRI International by the Law Enforcement Assistance Administration.

innovations.title: FRASTA (FRacture Surface Topography Analysis)
innovations.detail: SRI International developed a technology system to quantify and interpret material fatigue using fracture surface topography.

innovations.title: Human Exposure to Atmospheric Concentrations of Selected Chemicals
innovations.detail: SRI and the EPA compiled a report on the effect of four pollutants on human respiration.

innovations.title: EPA testing
innovations.detail: SRI test methods have been used in EPA testing since 1982.

innovations.title: TCP/IP protocol
innovations.detail: The development in 1982 of the TCP/IP protocol is still the standard protocol for the internet today.

innovations.title: ARPANET became part of the Military Network
innovations.detail: By 1983 ARPANET became part of the Military Network, the Defense Data Network and NSFNet.

innovations.title: RCA demonstrated its proprietary solid-state imagers at the NAB Convention
innovations.detail: RCA showed its experimental solid state imagers to an invited audience at the National Association of Broadcasters convention.

innovations.title: Reflex Transmission Imaging
innovations.detail: Philip Green and his colleagues at SRI International refined ultrasound using RTI to add the capability to generate high resolution imaging.

innovations.title: the company was given an Emmy award for Outstanding Technical Achievement
innovations.detail: The company received an Emmy award for Outstanding Technical Achievement for the solid state CCD work.

innovations.title: Tirapazamine
innovations.detail: Tirapazamine was developed in 1986 by SRI International in collaboration with researchers from Stanford Cancer Institute.

innovations.title: Reaction of Chlorine Nitrate with Hydrogen Chloride and Water at Antarctic Stratospheric Temperatures
innovations.detail: A team including SRI postdoctoral researcher Margaret Tolbert published a landmark paper on how chlorofluorocarbons release active chlorine that destroys ozone.

innovations.title: DARPA speech and natural language workshop
innovations.detail: The workshop was used as a platform to describe the technology behind DECIPHER.

innovations.title: Foliage-Penetrating Radar as a technology was advanced by SRI
innovations.detail: SRI advanced foliage penetrating radar technology during this decade for military use.

innovations.title: prototype
innovations.detail: A prototype was delivered in early 1994 that created pattern recognition algorithms fitted to the needs of live action TV.

innovations.title: Da Vinci/surgical robots + Taurus robotic system
innovations.detail: Intuitive Surgical, Inc., a SRI Ventures spin off, licensed SRI robotic surgery technology to commercialize the DaVinci Surgical System.

innovations.title: SRI created a comprehensive study sample of twins
innovations.detail: In 1995, SRI created a comprehensive study sample of twins that was turned into a community based registry, the Twin Research Registry (TRR).

innovations.title: SRI Language Modeling Toolkit (SRILM)
innovations.detail: It provides tools to build and apply statistical language models for speech recognition, statistical tagging and segmentation, and machine translation.

innovations.title: Charles Schwab & Co., Inc., used Nuance's speech recognition technology
innovations.detail: It allowed customers to receive stock quotes over the telephone.

innovations.title: FoxTrack Puck
innovations.detail: A technology used in Ice Hockey to place a glowing blue line around the puck so viewers could track it as it moved over the ice.

innovations.title: advanced address recognition system
innovations.detail: USPS deployed SRI's advanced address recognition system, which improved sorting rates by 12 percent.

innovations.title: first large scale commercial dialog system for United Parcel Services (UPS)
innovations.detail: UPS used the voice recognition platform to handle very large numbers of inquiries about package status.

innovations.title: first-down yellow line
innovations.detail: On September 27, 1998, ESPN's Sunday Night Football broadcast carried the first-down yellow line.

innovations.title: Video Mosaicing/ Video Brush
innovations.detail: SRI received an R and D 100 award for its video mosaicking technology in 1998.

innovations.title: Visual advertising insertion
innovations.detail: The first down yellow line made augmented reality real for sports fans in 1998.

innovations.title: Targretin
innovations.detail: SRI brought to the world several important cancer drugs including Targretin in 1999, used to treat cutaneous T cell lymphoma.

innovations.title: Targretin® (Bexarotene)
innovations.detail: In 1999, the FDA approved the use of Targretin® to treat cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.

innovations.title: SRI International submitted a proposal to build the world's first, relocatable Atmospheric Observatory
innovations.detail: SRI International submitted a proposal to build the world's first, relocatable Atmospheric Observatory.

innovations.title: Centibots ,  coordinated robots
innovations.detail: Centibots were designed to act as a swarm that communicate with each other and make decisions.

innovations.title: this project changed the original scope and became the AMISR
innovations.detail: In 2002, this project changed the original scope and became the AMISR.

innovations.title: CALO
innovations.detail: CALO was a collaborative effort led by SRI International, involving more than 300 researchers from 22 premier research institutions over five years, beginning in 2003.

innovations.title: spun-out a company, Artificial Muscle, Inc. (AMI)
innovations.detail: SRI International spun out a company called Artificial Muscle, Inc. that went on to commercialize SRI patented EPAM technology.

innovations.title: SRI International was awarded $22 million
innovations.detail: SRI International was awarded $22 million in 2003 to develop a personalized cognitive assistant under the PAL program.

innovations.title: the National Science Board approved funding
innovations.detail: The National Science Board approved funding in 2003, for four years, up to a total of 44 million dollars.

innovations.title: Actuator Technology Product Innovation of the Year Award
innovations.detail: AMI won the Frost and Sullivan Actuator Technology Product Innovation of the Year Award for their Universal Muscle Actuator.

innovations.title: Iris Biometrics
innovations.detail: Sarnoff Corporation, now part of SRI, developed Iris on the Move, a biometric solution that used iris recognition.

innovations.title: The Amazing Race: Mobile Text Messaging challenge
innovations.detail: Nuance pitted their speech recognition technology against the world's fastest texter.

innovations.title: Apple acquired Siri
innovations.detail: In 2010, Apple acquired Siri and an integrated version of the digital assistant appeared in the iPhone 4S in 2011.

innovations.title: Augmented reality binoculars
innovations.detail: SRI began research into using augmented reality within a set of binoculars back in 2010.

innovations.title: Bayer MaterialScience LLC acquired Artificial Muscle, Inc. (AMI)
innovations.detail: Bayer MaterialScience LLC acquired Artificial Muscle, Inc. and one technology from this acquisition was used to develop highly realistic haptic feedback for gaming.

innovations.title: appeared in the iPhone 4S
innovations.detail: In 2010, Apple acquired Siri and an integrated version of the digital assistant appeared in the iPhone 4S in 2011.

innovations.title: Seismic (Warrior Web)
innovations.detail: SRI began collaborating with DARPA in the Warrior Web Program to develop a robotic exosuit capable of enhancing a soldier muscles.

innovations.title: Video Brush
innovations.detail: SRI's Video Brush software was licensed to Google for use in Android smart phones in 2011.

innovations.title: shared their research at an Institute for Electrical and Electronic Engineers (IEEE) conference on mixed and augmented reality
innovations.detail: The Computer Vision Technologies Laboratory team presented its augmented reality binoculars research at an IEEE conference and in an IEEE publication.

innovations.title: Augmented Reality Binoculars
innovations.detail: The work appeared in IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics, volume 21, number 5, pages 611 to 623.

innovations.title: Abacus Drive
innovations.detail: The Abacus Drive is a fixed ratio rotary transmission gear system designed for use in robotics to facilitate smooth robotic movement.

innovations.title: demonstrated the capabilities of the Abacus Drive
innovations.detail: SRI engineers demonstrated the capabilities of the Abacus Drive at the 12th Annual RoboBusiness conference and trade show at the San Jose Convention Center.

innovations.title: MOTOBOT
innovations.detail: MOTOBOT became the world first autonomous motorcycle riding humanoid robot in 2016.

innovations.title: FOX Three
innovations.detail: Developed in 2017, FOX Three has since been used to develop new immunotherapies to further help cancer patients.

innovations.title: MOTOBOT took on Rossi
innovations.detail: In 2017, MOTOBOT took on Rossi but was pipped at the post by its human counterpart.

innovations.title: the NG911 NOW coalition presented a report to Congress on the next generation 911 (NG911) service
innovations.detail: The page states that in 2018 the NG911 NOW coalition presented a report to Congress on the next generation 911 service.

innovations.title: SRI transferred the TRR into the hands of Stanford Medicine
innovations.detail: In 2019, SRI transferred the TRR into the hands of Stanford Medicine; at that point, there were 6,208 individual twins in the registry.

innovations.title: FOX Three Molecular Guidance System
innovations.detail: SRI International solved the delivery of large molecular drugs with their unique guidance system, known as the FOX Three Molecular Guidance System (MGS).

innovations.title: Nomura SRI Innovation Center (NSIC)
innovations.detail: In September 2020, SRI and Nomura Holdings announced the creation of the Nomura SRI Innovation Center as a home for member companies to refine existing corporate innovation activities and develop new innovation initiatives.

innovations.title: NSIC began
innovations.detail: Located within the heart of Silicon Valley at SRI's Menlo Park campus, NSIC began in July 2021 and has had 17 member companies participate in their programming.

innovations.title: The DiaCyt CNS (Central Nervous System) drug delivery platform was announced
innovations.detail: The DiaCyt CNS (Central Nervous System) drug delivery platform was announced in 2021 as a system that helps deliver drugs to the CNS that would otherwise prevent biologic therapies such as antibodies and gene therapies being used.

profile_text.body:
SRI International is an independent nonprofit research and development institute headquartered at 333 Ravenswood Ave, Menlo Park, CA 94025. It was founded in 1946 as Stanford Research Institute and has been independent since 1970. It acquired Sarnoff Corp. (formerly RCA Labs) in 1987 and the Palo Alto Research Center (PARC) in 2023. It has about 1,500 researchers and professionals. The company describes itself as a global leader in R&D with deep roots in Silicon Valley, and says it works in quantum, AI, human-machine collaboration, precision medicine, education, and sustainability. Innovations it lists include ARPANET (1969), internetworking (1970s), handwriting recognition and pen input (1964), telerobotic surgery (1990s) and Siri (2000s).

David Parekh is Chief Executive Officer. Suresh Sunderrajan is Chief Financial Officer, John McIntire is Chief Legal Officer, Joann Lime is Chief Human Resources Officer, and Michael Page is Chief Information Officer. Division presidents include Kathlynn Brown (Biosciences), John Crowe (Advanced Technology and Systems), Todd A. Grindal (SRI Education), Steve Perna (Integrated Systems and Solutions), and Dimitra Vergyri (Information and Computing Sciences, and director of the Speech Technology and Research Laboratory). David Motley is Chairman of the Board, and directors include Stefan Heck, Charles Mathis, Marshall Mohr, Ellen Ochoa, Ellen M. Pawlikowski, Rengarajan Ramesh, and Steven Walker.

No lawsuits are recorded for the company. It has no tracked products and no MCP servers in this record. Its recorded legal exposure is in California, with a count of 281.
